prompt:
[A]
 Although it is true that many animal populations grow exponentially for a period of time, it must be remembered that the food available to sustain the population is limited and the population will level off because of this. One mathematical model to describe a population that grows exponentially at the beginning and then levels off to a limiting value, L, is the logistic model. The equation for this model is P = aL/[a + (L - a)e^(-kLt)], where t represents time, P represents the size of the population, a is the size of the population at t = 0, L is the limiting value, and k is a mathematical constant.
 a. Suppose that a biologist starts a cell colony with 100 cells and finds that the limiting size of the colony is 10 000 cells. If the constant k = 0.0001, draw a graph to illustrate this population, where t is in days.
 b. At what point in time does the cell colony stop growing exponentially? How large is the colony at this point?
 c. Compare the growth rate of the colony at the end of day 3 with the growth rate at the end of day 8. Explain what is happening.
